ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Lili Boulanger — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Review at week 4 of risankizumab, on the day of the second induction infusion

text.paragraph: Review at week 4 of risankizumab, on the day of the second infusion. [S]

Ms. Boulanger had her first risankizumab infusion and intravenous iron four weeks ago without reaction and has her second infusion today. Her stools are down to two or three a day, soft, with no night-time stool, and the cramps are mild (Harvey-Bradshaw Index 5). She is on 20 mg of prednisone, falling to 15 mg this week, and has noticed a rounder face and lighter sleep. She has gained 1.6 kg with the supplements. The mycobacterial culture from her biopsies shows no growth after five weeks; the final report is due next week. She is rehearsing for her concert at the end of the month and composing most mornings. [S]

Crohn disease of the terminal ileum and colon (ileocolitis), Montreal A2 L3 B1 without perianal disease, moderate to severe: deep ileal ulcers over 15 cm and patchy colonic ulcers, SES-CD 14, Harvey-Bradshaw Index 11; intestinal tuberculosis excluded by negative interferon-gamma release assay, normal chest X-ray, and biopsies negative for acid-fast bacilli, TB PCR, and mycobacterial culture; synthetic modern diagnosis linked to her documented chronic intestinal illness, whose historical diagnosis is not settled

S — Synthetic diagnosis confirmed within the modern episode; her historical illness is documented (D), but whether it was intestinal tuberculosis or Crohn disease remains a retrospective interpretation (R) and is disputed.
